issues.legal_issue: A government declaration that a land acquisition serves a public purpose is not open to challenge absent a collateral purpose or a colourable exercise of power.
material_facts: The land was acquired at public expense to enable the establishment of a manufacturing industry.
The government declared that the acquisition served a public purpose.
The challengers did not establish that the acquisition was for a collateral purpose or involved a colourable exercise of power.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was for a public purpose, and the government’s declaration was not open to challenge on the facts.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 6(3) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the government’s declaration that an acquisition is for a public purpose is conclusive evidence that the land is needed for that purpose, subject to challenge where there is a colourable exercise of power. Whether starting an industry is in the public interest is essentially for the government to decide. The Court relied on Smt. Somavanti v. State of Punjab and Raja Anand Brahma Shah v. State of U.P.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_land_acquisition and government_declared_public_purpose and not proven_collateral_or_colorable_purpose

predicates.appeal_challenging_land_acquisition: A party appealed a decision in a proceeding challenging a land acquisition.
predicates.government_declared_public_purpose: The government declared that the acquisition was for a public purpose.
predicates.proven_collateral_or_colorable_purpose: The challenger established that the acquisition was for a collateral purpose or was a colourable exercise of power.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a land acquisition declared to serve a public purpose and no collateral purpose or colourable exercise of power is established, the declaration is not open to challenge.

issues.legal_issue: Acquisition for a company need not proceed under the statutory provisions governing company acquisitions when the State contributes toward the acquisition cost.
material_facts: The acquisition was made at public expense, and the State contributed toward its cost.
The pleadings did not permit the challengers to contend that the State had made no contribution.
issues.conclusion: It was not necessary to conduct the acquisition under Part VII of the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Where the State contributes toward the cost of acquisition, it is not necessary to proceed under Part VII of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. The Court relied on Smt. Somavanti v. State of Punjab.

predicates.appeal_challenging_land_acquisition: A party appealed a decision in a proceeding challenging a land acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_benefits_company: The acquisition was for the benefit of a company.
predicates.state_contributed_to_acquisition_cost: The State contributed toward the cost of acquiring the land.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an acquisition benefiting a company and the State contributed toward its cost, the company-specific acquisition procedure is not required.

issues.legal_issue: Urgent acquisition procedure is justified where the circumstances show urgency, with the government’s assessment of urgency entitled to weight but not treated as conclusive.
material_facts: The project had a government-imposed completion deadline that had been extended to a date soon after the acquisition notifications.
The project required land to be acquired promptly to meet that deadline.
The government formed the view that urgent steps were needed and invoked the urgent acquisition procedure.
Any earlier delay by the government or the project party did not determine whether urgency existed when the notification was issued.
issues.conclusion: There was urgency on the facts, so recourse to the urgent acquisition procedure was justified.
issues.legal_principle: The government’s conclusion that urgency exists is entitled to weight, though it is not conclusive. Whether urgency exists is assessed in light of the circumstances at the time of the notification; earlier lethargy by the government or the interested party is not decisive.

predicates.appeal_challenging_urgent_land_acquisiti: A party appealed a decision in a proceeding challenging the use of an urgent procedure to acquire land.
predicates.government_found_urgent_need: The government formed the view that the acquisition was urgently needed.
predicates.project_deadline_required_prompt_acquisi: The project’s completion deadline made prompt acquisition of the land necessary.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an urgent land acquisition, the government found an urgent need, and a project deadline required prompt acquisition, the urgent procedure is justified.

issues.legal_issue: The general urgent-purpose provision is not restricted by the ejusdem generis rule to the particular categories in adjacent provisions where the provisions involve different decision-makers and conditions.
material_facts: The challengers argued that the general wording of the urgent-purpose provision should be limited by the specific categories in adjacent provisions.
The adjacent provisions assigned acquisition decisions to different authorities and imposed conditions that differed from those in the general provision.
The general provision plainly allowed urgent acquisition for a public purpose where the appropriate government considered the purpose to be of urgent importance.
issues.conclusion: The ejusdem generis rule did not apply, and the general provision was not confined to the categories in the adjacent provisions.
issues.legal_principle: Ejusdem generis is a rule of construction applied cautiously and only where the specific words establish a distinct genus and the legislative context supports restricting the general words. Clear and unambiguous language reflecting clear legislative intent is given its ordinary meaning. The Court relied on State of Bombay v. Ali Gulshan, Lilavati Bai v. State of Bombay, and K.K. Kochuni v. State of Madras and Kerala.

predicates.appeal_challenging_urgent_land_acquisiti: A party appealed a decision in a proceeding challenging the use of an urgent procedure to acquire land.
predicates.general_provision_has_clear_meaning: The general provision plainly states the circumstances in which it applies.
predicates.adjacent_provisions_use_different_author: Adjacent provisions assign decisions to different authorities and impose conditions different from those in the general provision.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an urgent land acquisition, the general provision has a clear meaning, and adjacent provisions use different authorities and conditions, the general provision is not limited to the adjacent categories.
